Minimum Requirements (Required)
Education: Bachelor of Science (B.S.) degree from an accredited college or university in fisheries, aquatic science, hatchery management, or a closely related field.
Experience: Practical experience working in fisheries, aquatic systems, or hatchery operations.

Preferred Qualifications
Experience: Two (2) years of demonstrated hands-on experience in hatchery operations.
Specialized Experience: Direct experience operating, maintaining, and troubleshooting Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS).
Education/Experience Substitution: A Master's degree in a related field may substitute for one (1) year of the preferred operational experience.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:
Required Qualifications
Technical & Mechanical Systems: Strong practical knowledge of mechanical systems, including small engines, electric motors, HVAC, and plumbing, with the demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex mechanical and biological issues.
Aquaculture & Systems Knowledge: Working knowledge of Great Lakes fisheries, natural resource management, and aquaculture infrastructure-specifically Recirculating Aquaculture Systems (RAS).
Field & Operational Skills: Proven experience operating and trailering boats, conducting field sampling, collecting gametes, handling fish, and adhering to strict sanitary/biosecurity protocols.
Software & Data Proficiency: Demonstrated competency with spreadsheet, database, mapping, and analytical software (e.g., Microsoft Office, Access, R, QGIS, ArcGIS).
Problem Solving & Adaptability: Ability to troubleshoot challenges independently for extended periods, as well as collaborate effectively within a team environment.
Communication: Excel in a team-oriented environment.

Preferred Qualifications
Specialized Aquaculture: Direct experience with live feed cultivation (zooplankton, Artemia, algae) and the rearing of warm- and cold-water fish species (specifically Great Lakes salmonids, percids, and lake sturgeon).
Tribal & Agency Collaboration: Prior experience collaborating with Tribal organizations, natural resource agencies, or inter-departmental teams.

Mobility & Posture: Regularly required to stand, walk, reach, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl when working around rearing units, raceways, and field gear.

occasionally lift and/or move loads exceeding 50 pounds using team lifts or mechanical assistance.

Description
 The Opportunity

One Hundred Miles (OHM) is a coastal conservation nonprofit organization working to protect Georgia’s coast through advocacy, education, and community engagement. Since its founding in 2013, OHM has grown from a bold idea into an influential, highly respected organization with a talented staff, an engaged board, a broad network of advocates, strong philanthropic support, trusted relationships, and a record of impact in protecting the landscapes, wildlife, communities, and quality of life that make coastal Georgia extraordinary. You can read more about its recent accomplishments, staff, financial stewardship, and current issues in the FY2025 Annual Report.

After more than a decade of leadership by its founding leader, OHM is preparing for an important transition in recruiting the next President & CEO. This leader will inherit an organization in strong financial and organizational health. The opportunity is to understand what has made the organization successful, preserve and build on those strengths, and help a maturing organization move confidently into its next era at an urgent moment for Georgia’s coast.

OHM’s next leader must bring an unwavering commitment to the mission along with the judgment to know how best to advance it. That will require both courage and collaboration: a willingness to take bold positions when the stakes demand it, while also building coalitions and finding common ground with partners who may not share OHM’s perspective on every issue.

This is not a caretaker role; OHM is seeking a leader prepared to build on its success, make consequential decisions, and lead with conviction. The next leader will honor OHM’s legacy and strengths while bringing their own experience, relationships, instincts, and leadership style to the work. Success will require both continuity and evolution.

The Organization

OHM’s vision is a future in which coastal Georgia’s people, wildlife, and environment thrive. Its work spans responsible development, land use, water, wetlands, climate resilience, wildlife, environmental health, education, and community engagement. OHM combines grassroots organizing, public education, policy and legislative advocacy, scientific information, relationship building, and coalition leadership.

The organization has built an advocacy network of more than 43,000 people and has demonstrated an ability to work locally, statewide, and with national partners. OHM is bold in taking a stand on issues and does not shy away from litigation, public advocacy, or grassroots organizing.

At the same time, OHM recognizes that durable conservation requires collaboration. Georgia’s coast is a distinctive place, shaped by close-knit communities, local and state politics, long-standing relationships, and constituencies that may see the same issues very differently. OHM’s strategic plan calls for finding common ground with people and organizations whose interests intersect with coastal conservation and for strengthening the capacity of partners across the region.

OHM is a financially strong organization with an engaged and active board, 15 full-time staff working from offices in Brunswick, Savannah, and Darien, and a growing annual operating budget approaching $2 million. The organization has also recently completed a successful $6 million capital campaign, One Hundred Miles, One Coast, reflecting strong philanthropic support and confidence in OHM’s mission and future. Its board and professional staff both bring environmental expertise across conservation, advocacy, education, philanthropy, communications, and operations, providing the next President & CEO with a strong foundation from which to lead the organization’s next chapter.

The organization is guided by core values of Innovation, Resilience, Justice & Equity, Transparency, and Engagement. Internally, OHM has articulated expectations and team values of Integrity, Initiative, Communication, and One Team. Together, these values reflect an organization that is courageous, accountable, collaborative, open to learning, and deeply connected to the people and places it serves.

OHM’s current strategic plan provides a clear framework for the work ahead. Priorities include strengthening the broader conservation movement, advancing climate resilience, advocating for responsible development, addressing threats to water, wildlife, air quality, and public health, expanding opportunities for people to experience and protect the coast, and continuing to strengthen OHM itself through thoughtful growth and investment in its people.

The Mandate

The President & CEO will be responsible for leading OHM into its next chapter. The role requires the urgency, courage, integrity, collaborative orientation, and mission focus that have defined the organization. The work will require an executive who can lead internally and externally; manage a strong team; make thoughtful choices about priorities; raise resources; engage in advocacy; and represent OHM with credibility across the coast and beyond.

Key priorities will include:

Translate OHM’s strategic plan into operational priorities and measurable progress; articulate a compelling, forward-looking vision for the coast; and remain responsive to urgent needs as they emerge.
Lead a thoughtful transition from a long-serving founding executive. Listen first, understand the history and relationships that matter, and build trust while making significant changes.
Build on organizational strengths while continuing to strengthen systems, structures, role clarity, and internal communication as OHM matures, with a collaborative spirit but willingness to lead decisively.
Lead, develop, and retain a talented staff. Set clear expectations, delegate meaningfully, coach and develop people, address problems directly, and create accountability without diminishing initiative.
Maintain the organization’s strong financial position and bring the discipline to align people, programs, resources, and strategy.
Partner as an integral part of fundraising and the primary external ambassador, expanding OHM’s visibility and circle of support. Build relationships with donors and funders, make a compelling case for investment, and effectively engage with staff and the Board in sustaining and growing philanthropic support.
Build credibility across communities, understand the history behind relationships and disagreements, and work effectively with people whose political, economic, or conservation perspectives differ.
Engage in advocacy and understand what it means to litigate, lobby, and educate. Bring strong judgment about when to push, when to listen, when to negotiate, when to convene, and when a long-term relationship may matter as much as a short-term win.
Work in close partnership with the Board, using its experience, relationships, and commitment while providing the clarity and leadership necessary for strong governance.

The President and CEO must be able to build trust across ideological, political, geographic, racial, socioeconomic, and professional differences. They should be able to find common ground without sacrificing principle, and to build coalitions around shared interests in the spirit of conservation. With this, the President and CEO must determine where OHM should lead, where it should partner, and where its resources can have the greatest impact.

This is a time of tremendous growth and development on Georgia’s coast, alongside a changing policy and regulatory environment. There is urgency in OHM’s work, and that work must continue confidently through this important leadership transition.

The Ideal Candidate

There are multiple pathways to this role. The next President & CEO may come from conservation, environmental advocacy, law or public policy, a land or water organization, philanthropy, civic leadership, government, community-based advocacy, or another mission-driven environment. What matters most is the combination of leadership ability, sound judgment, management strength, relationship building, fundraising capacity, and authentic commitment to the mission.

The strongest candidates will bring:

A genuine commitment to coastal conservation and to the diverse people, wildlife, communities, and landscapes of Georgia’s coast.
Significant organizational leadership experience and the judgment to lead through a consequential transition.
A strong record as a manager of people, including the ability to set direction, develop talent, delegate, communicate clearly, and create healthy accountability.
Significant credibility in conservation, advocacy, public policy, and/or civic engagement, with a record of ability to succeed due to influence, persistence, and sound judgment.
Experience using or working alongside a range of advocacy tools, including litigation, legislative and policy advocacy, grassroots organizing, coalition-building, and education.
Fundraising ability and comfort building relationships with individual donors, foundations, institutional partners, and other supporters.
Financial and operational fluency, including an understanding of the legal and regulatory considerations governing nonprofit advocacy, or the ability to master them quickly.
Strong communication and presentation skills and an effective public presence.
Courage, steadiness, resilience, humility, and pragmatism.
A willingness to listen, learn quickly, share credit, take responsibility, and work with colleagues who bring deep expertise of their own.

Prior experience in Georgia or on the southern coast will be valuable, but it is not a requirement. Candidates who are new to the region will need to demonstrate how they will learn the coast quickly and humbly.

Relationships

Relationships are fundamental to how OHM gets its work done. The President & CEO will work with staff and Board members, donors and philanthropic partners, elected and appointed officials, agency leaders, conservation organizations, business and civic leaders, community advocates, scientists, attorneys, property owners, residents, and others whose interests intersect along the coast.

Reports to: Board
Manages: Staff
Collaborates with: Diverse and varied organizations, communities, policy-makers

Location

This is a place-based leadership role. OHM’s main office is in Brunswick with additional offices in Savannah and Darien. The President & CEO must maintain a meaningful, on-the-ground presence in each office and in communities throughout coastal Georgia with occasional additional travel. This is not a role to lead from a distance.

Compensation

Compensation is expected to be in the mid-$100s, commensurate with experience and qualifications. One Hundred Miles offers a competitive benefits package.

Description
The Alaska Department of Fish and Game, Division of Wildlife Conservation is recruiting
 for a Wildlife Biologist 2 (Dillingham Assistant Area Wildlife Biologist) located in Dillingham, Alaska!

What You Will Be Doing:
This position, based in Dillingham, serves as the Assistant Area Wildlife Management Biologist for western and southwestern Alaska managing wildlife populations, in portions of the Alaska Range, Aleutian Islands, and Wood River mountains (Game Management Units 9, 10, and 17). The assistant area biologist assists in evaluating, planning, and conducting management and research activities (including intensive management) to benefit game, furbearer and other terrestrial wildlife resources.

Our Mission, Values and Culture: 
This position fulfills the division’s mission in the Central-Southwest Region 4 to conserve and enhance Alaska's wildlife and habitats and provide for a wide range of public uses and benefits. The incumbent maintains and enhances opportunities to hunt, trap and view wildlife while providing opportunities for Alaskans to gain knowledge of and appreciation for Alaska's wildlife, its management, and ways to interact with wildlife safely and ethically.

The Alaska Department of Fish & Game strives for a diverse and inclusive workforce where safety and well-being are paramount and employees at all levels promote a culture where everyone is valued, treated equitably, and treated respectfully. 


Benefits of Joining Our Team: 
This position offers a challenging and fulfilling, professional opportunity to assist in the management of world-class, wildlife resources, including six caribou herds, for the Dillingham and King Salmon management areas (Game Management Units 9, 10, and 17) to meet DWC’s mission. This position will work directly with management and research biologists to grow professionally and gain experience assessing wildlife resources and managing a diversity of wildlife for long-term conservation. Residents living in these communities enjoy abundant opportunities to engage in hunting, fishing, gathering and numerous other outdoor recreational pursuits in an area with record salmon runs and pristine wilderness. There is no state income tax in Alaska.

The Working Environment You Can Expect:
Based in Dillingham (a significant rural population center), this position assists in administering wildlife management programs, including the Mulchatna caribou herd and coastal brown bears, requiring field time away from duty station (up to 1–2 weeks at a time). Daily work environment spans from report writing, data analysis, and interacting with stakeholders to conducting wildlife surveys, investigations, and capturing and handling wildlife.
This position is based in Dillingham (Unit 17) but will also have responsibilities in the King Salmon Management Area (Units 9 & 10).
Requires frequent travel within the management area and state.
Requires the use of firearms and the ability to fly in small fixed-wing and rotor aircraft in mountainous environments.
Requires occasional work at nights and on weekends.

Who We Are Looking For:
We are looking for an individual with the following knowledge, skills, and abilities:
Knowledge of the life history of wildlife species in Alaska and a working knowledge of wildlife biology, ecology, management, and population dynamics.
Experience capturing, immobilizing, and performing physical examinations of various large mammal species.
Experience collecting data via aerial and ground investigations, working with databases, preparing data analyses and summaries, and writing technical reports and presentations.
Proficiency with firearms and experience/ability to fly in small aircraft in mountainous terrain.
Experience in addressing public and stakeholder inquiries on complex issues or regulations through both oral and written communication, such as explaining trapping and hunting regulations, processes for obtaining hunting permits, regulatory procedures, intensive management, and matters concerning public access.

 go to the following link: https://www.governmentjobs.com/careers/Alaska/classspecs

This position may be in possession of, or have access to, firearms/ammunition. Alaska State Peace Officer certification

Firearms training certification

certification as an Associate or Certified Wildlife Biologist by The Wildlife Society or similar professional organization (recommended)

Minimum Qualifications


A bachelor’s degree from an accredited college in biology, a branch of biology, limnology, biometrics, oceanography, forestry, or natural resource management.
AND
One year of professional level biologist experience. The required professional biologist experience is met by service as a Wildlife Biologist 1, Fishery Biologist 1, or Habitat Biologist 1 with the State of Alaska or the equivalent with another employer.


Substitutions:
A bachelor’s degree from an accredited college that includes or is supplemented by the following credit hours will substitute for the degree in a specific field:
• at least 24 semester hours (36 quarter hours) in biology, a branch of biology, limnology, biometrics, oceanography, forestry, or natural resource management (excluding courses that focus on agricultural husbandry techniques, human population dynamics, or the design and manipulation of landscapes), of which 16 semester hours (24 quarter hours) are upper division courses; and
• at least 12 semester hours (16 quarter hours) in any combination of two or more of the following: chemistry, physics, mathematics, statistics, geology, hydrology, or GIS.


A master's degree from an accredited college in biology, a branch of biology, limnology, biometrics, oceanography, forestry or natural resource management, will substitute for the required year of professional level biologist experience.

“Upper division courses” means courses that are specialized, in-depth and advanced. Such courses emphasize problem-solving, analytical thinking skills, and theoretical applications, with depth and rigor in a discipline’s theories and methods; specialization in a particular field or profession; refinement of general education; and/or development of specific intellectual and professional skills. This position, based in Dillingham, serves as the Assistant Area Wildlife Management Biologist for western and southwestern Alaska managing wildlife populations, in portions of the Alaska Range, Aleutian Islands, and Wood River mountains (Game Management Units 9, 10, and 17). The assistant area biologist assists in evaluating, planning, and conducting management and research activities (including intensive management) to benefit game, furbearer and other terrestrial wildlife resources.

Our Mission, Values and Culture: 
This position fulfills the division’s mission in the Central-Southwest Region 4 to conserve and enhance Alaska's wildlife and habitats and provide for a wide range of public uses and benefits. The incumbent maintains and enhances opportunities to hunt, trap and view wildlife while providing opportunities for Alaskans to gain knowledge of and appreciation for Alaska's wildlife, its management, and ways to interact with wildlife safely and ethically.

The Alaska Department of Fish & Game strives for a diverse and inclusive workforce where safety and well-being are paramount and employees at all levels promote a culture where everyone is valued, treated equitably, and treated respectfully. 


Benefits of Joining Our Team: 
This position offers a challenging and fulfilling, professional opportunity to assist in the management of world-class, wildlife resources, including six caribou herds, for the Dillingham and King Salmon management areas (Game Management Units 9, 10, and 17) to meet DWC’s mission. This position will work directly with management and research biologists to grow professionally and gain experience assessing wildlife resources and managing a diversity of wildlife for long-term conservation. Residents living in these communities enjoy abundant opportunities to engage in hunting, fishing, gathering and numerous other outdoor recreational pursuits in an area with record salmon runs and pristine wilderness. There is no state income tax in Alaska.

The Working Environment You Can Expect:
Based in Dillingham (a significant rural population center), this position assists in administering wildlife management programs, including the Mulchatna caribou herd and coastal brown bears, requiring field time away from duty station (up to 1–2 weeks at a time). Daily work environment spans from report writing, data analysis, and interacting with stakeholders to conducting wildlife surveys, investigations, and capturing and handling wildlife.
This position is based in Dillingham (Unit 17) but will also have responsibilities in the King Salmon Management Area (Units 9 & 10).
Requires frequent travel within the management area and state.
Requires the use of firearms and the ability to fly in small fixed-wing and rotor aircraft in mountainous environments.
Requires occasional work at nights and on weekends.

Who We Are Looking For:
We are looking for an individual with the following knowledge, skills, and abilities:
Knowledge of the life history of wildlife species in Alaska and a working knowledge of wildlife biology, ecology, management, and population dynamics.
Experience capturing, immobilizing, and performing physical examinations of various large mammal species.
Experience collecting data via aerial and ground investigations, working with databases, preparing data analyses and summaries, and writing technical reports and presentations.
Proficiency with firearms and experience/ability to fly in small aircraft in mountainous terrain.
Experience in addressing public and stakeholder inquiries on complex issues or regulations through both oral and written communication, such as explaining trapping and hunting regulations, processes for obtaining hunting permits, regulatory procedures, intensive management, and matters concerning public access.

certification as an Associate or Certified Wildlife Biologist by The Wildlife Society or similar professional organization (recommended)

Minimum Qualifications


A bachelor’s degree from an accredited college in biology, a branch of biology, limnology, biometrics, oceanography, forestry, or natural resource management.
AND
One year of professional level biologist experience. The required professional biologist experience is met by service as a Wildlife Biologist 1, Fishery Biologist 1, or Habitat Biologist 1 with the State of Alaska or the equivalent with another employer.


Substitutions:
A bachelor’s degree from an accredited college that includes or is supplemented by the following credit hours will substitute for the degree in a specific field:
• at least 24 semester hours (36 quarter hours) in biology, a branch of biology, limnology, biometrics, oceanography, forestry, or natural resource management (excluding courses that focus on agricultural husbandry techniques, human population dynamics, or the design and manipulation of landscapes), of which 16 semester hours (24 quarter hours) are upper division courses; and
• at least 12 semester hours (16 quarter hours) in any combination of two or more of the following: chemistry, physics, mathematics, statistics, geology, hydrology, or GIS.


A master's degree from an accredited college in biology, a branch of biology, limnology, biometrics, oceanography, forestry or natural resource management, will substitute for the required year of professional level biologist experience.

This DNR Wildlife Temporary Worker position is expected to perform a variety of semi-skilled maintenance and technical tasks at a wildlife management unit. The employee is expected to display a high level of initiative and commitment towards completing assignments efficiently. Employees in this position will work with other wildlife unit personnel and be under the general direction of the Wildlife Biologist.

Description
Are you looking to break into the field of conservation, but don’t know where to start? Consider spending 2027 in beautiful New Hampshire and join the Lakes Region Conservation Corps (LRCC), an AmeriCorps service program that develops skills and experiences for the next generation of conservation professionals. LRCC members are the driving force behind many of the conservation efforts of New Hampshire's Lakes Region.  The LRCC full year program features 3 actively recruiting host sites (see site details below), each offering unique experiences and opportunities to members.


Key responsibilities may include:
-Engage both youth and adults in environmental education and outreach programs.
-Recruit and lead volunteer crews.
-Work toward the eradication of invasive species in the lakes and watershed.
-Maintain and construct regional trail networks.
-And more, dependent on host site!


Host Sites:
Each host site operates independently and has additional, specialized duties and experiences. Highlights of each site are included below, but applicants are encouraged to learn more about each host site here https://www.lakesregionconservationcorps.org/lrcc-sites

Squam Lakes Association (10 positions available)
Holderness, NH
The Squam Lakes Association (SLA) provides hands-on conservation experience and certifications over a broad range of areas, building confidence to independently approach a variety of tasks in conservation, environmental education, and recreation resource management. Members will complete trainings, projects and tasks which include: water quality monitoring and testing, trail restoration, campsite caretaking, SCUBA diving to remove invasive variable milfoil, managing volunteers, and acting as an ambassador for the LRCC and SLA. 
 The Nature Conservancy (2 positions available)
New Market and Various other locations across NH
Members will work as a small team completing various land management tasks throughout NH. Members will have the opportunity to gain experience in ecological monitoring, data collection, trail maintenance, invasive species control, fire management, volunteer coordination and engaging with the public. Members can become federally certified NWCG Basic Wildland Firefighters. Housing is provided.

Mount Washington Observatory (2 position available)
North Conway, NH
Members serving at MWOBS support the development and presentation of educational programs for K-12 students and adult learners both in and out of the traditional classroom. Programs include school-day, after-school and field-trip-style programs for K-12 learners in addition to regularly supporting interpretative programming on the summit of Mount Washington. Housing is provided


All members have the opportunity to receive these trainings, certifications, and benefits:
-Wilderness First Aid & CPR certifications
-Living allowance; $914.80 bi-weekly ($20,400 aggregate)
-NH Commercial Boating License
-Housing provided
-Student loan forbearance and interest repayment for qualifying loans
-Segal Education Award upon successful completion of the program and 1700 hours: $7,395
-Additional trainings provided vary by host site.
-Health care coverage available

Minimum Qualifications as per AmeriCorps CNCS Guidelines:
-Must be 18 years of age by January 13, 2027
-Must be a US citizen, US national, or legal permanent resident
-Must clear all required national service criminal history checks
-Must be a high school graduate, GED recipient, or be working towards obtaining one prior to start of term of service
-Host sites may have additional requirements

Commitment:
January 13th, 2027 through November 19th, 2027. Members must complete at least 1700 hours over the course of the program in order to successfully complete the program and receive the Segal AmeriCorps Education Award.

Application Deadline:
Applications are reviewed in the order in which they are received and offers made on a rolling basis. Interested applicants are encouraged to apply early.

Apply Now:
https://www.lakesregionconservationcorps.org/apply-now

Description
The Biology Department at Adams State University invites applicants for a tenure-track assistant or associate professor position in anatomy and physiology. Primary responsibilities include teaching lecture and laboratory courses in human anatomy and physiology, animal physiology, and nutrition. Participation in General Biology, general education biology courses, or other core biology courses may also be required. While we are primarily a teaching-focused institution, tenure-track faculty are expected to conduct scholarly or creative activity and maintain currency in their field. The ability to involve undergraduate students in research is valued. Faculty also provide service to the department, university, and community. Faculty teaching loads are 12 credit hours per semester. With small class sizes, a diverse student population, and opportunities for one-on-one mentoring, our campus environment lends itself well to those who are interested in being a positive influence in the lives of students.  

Candidates should demonstrate that they possess (1) a commitment to student-centered instruction, 2) a knowledge of or willingness to develop skills in high-impact and inclusive pedagogy in the context of biology education, and 3) a plan for conducting research/scholarly activity at a primarily undergraduate institution. The successful candidate must demonstrate the ability to communicate effectively and collaborate with diverse faculty, staff, and students within the School of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics and across campus.  

Start Date: The position is available to start August 2027 

Mission of the Department 

The biology program provides an inclusive and empowering education that fosters curiosity, critical thinking, and a deep appreciation for the natural world. We support and inspire students in their pursuit of scientific excellence through innovative teaching, research, and community engagement. We are committed to creating a diverse community of scholars who will lead with compassion, innovation, and a commitment to advancing both science and social equity.   We recognize that women and people of color are often less likely to apply to a position if they don’t match 100% of the job qualifications. Don’t let that be the reason you miss out on this opportunity! We encourage you to apply if you can demonstrate many of these skills and competencies.  

Minimum Qualifications 
Ph.D. in Biology with a background in anatomy and physiology, ABD with expected completion date within 6 months of employment will be considered.
Demonstrated commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching and student-centered learning.
Demonstrates knowledge of, sensitivity to, and ability to work effectively with, the educational needs of individuals and groups with a diverse range of identities, cultures, backgrounds, and abilities
Evidence of responsiveness to and understanding of the racial, socioeconomic, academic, and cultural diversity of Adams State University’s student population, including students with different abilities (e.g. physical and or learning) as these factors relate to the need for equity-minded, inclusive practices within the classroom
Demonstrated commitment to honesty, efficacy, and collaboration.

Preferred Qualifications 
Experience teaching at the undergraduate level.
Knowledge of or experience with high-impact, active teaching strategies
Commitment to undergraduate laboratory instruction, including proficiency with physiology data collection software and experience with dissection of vertebrate animals and major organs.
Ability or experience working with historically under-served and/or underrepresented populations, and first-generation college students.
Ability or experience in the recruitment and/or retention of underrepresented students, including students of color.
Commitment to professional development, scholarship, and service to the university and community.
Demonstrated self-awareness of one's own cultural beliefs, perspectives, and privileges as a part of one's orientation towards teaching.
Demonstrated decision-making that is informed by research, data, and theory and that leverages students' unique cultures, experiences, and background as strengths.

Salary and Benefits 
The pay range for this position is $50,469-$63,086 for the assistant professor level and $58,862-$73,578 for those with experience at the associate professor level. Description
The Biology Department at Adams State University invites applicants for a tenure-track assistant or associate professor position in plant biology. We are seeking a broadly trained plant biologist to join an engaged and vibrant faculty committed to excellence in undergraduate education. Primary responsibilities include teaching multiple upper-division lecture and laboratory courses in plant ecology, plant systematics, plant physiology, mycology, and/or vegetation management. Participation in lower-division biology courses, including general biology, non-majors biology, ecology or evolution may also be required. While we are primarily an institution focused on teaching excellence, tenure-track faculty are expected to maintain currency in their field and conduct scholarly or creative activity. The ability to involve undergraduate students in research is valued. Faculty also provide service to the department, university, and community. With small class sizes, a diverse student population, and opportunities for one-on-one mentoring, our campus environment lends itself well to those who are interested in being a positive influence in the lives of students. 

Candidates should demonstrate that they possess (1) a commitment to student-centered instruction, 2) a knowledge of or willingness to develop skills in high-impact and inclusive pedagogy in the context of biology education, and 3) a plan for conducting research/scholarly activity at a primarily undergraduate institution. The successful candidate will demonstrate the ability to communicate effectively and collaborate with diverse faculty, staff, and students within the School of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics and across campus.  

Start Date: The position is available to start August 2027 

Mission of the Department 

The biology program provides an inclusive and empowering education that fosters curiosity, critical thinking, and a deep appreciation for the natural world. We support and inspire students in their pursuit of scientific excellence through innovative teaching, research, and community engagement. We are committed to creating a diverse community of scholars who will lead with compassion, innovation, and a commitment to advancing both science and social equity.   

We recognize that women and people of color are often less likely to apply to a position if they don’t match 100% of the job qualifications. Don’t let that be the reason you miss out on this opportunity! We encourage you to apply if you can demonstrate many of these skills and competencies.  

Minimum Qualifications 
Ph.D. in Biology with a background in botany/plant biology; or ABD with expected completion date within 6 months of employment.
Demonstrated commitment to excellence in undergraduate teaching and student-centered learning.
Demonstrates knowledge of, sensitivity to, and ability to work effectively with, the educational needs of individuals and groups with a diverse range of identities, cultures, backgrounds, and abilities
Evidence of responsiveness to and understanding of the racial, socioeconomic, academic, and cultural diversity of Adams State University’s student population, including students with different abilities (e.g. physical and or learning) as these factors relate to the need for equity minded, inclusive practices within the classroom
Demonstrated commitment to honesty, efficacy, and collaboration.

Preferred Qualifications 
Experience teaching at the undergraduate level
Knowledge of or experience with high-impact, active teaching strategies
Commitment to undergraduate inquiry-based laboratory and field-based instruction
Ability or experience working with historically under-served and/or underrepresented populations, and first-generation college students.
Ability or experience in the recruitment and/or retention of underrepresented students, including students of color.
Commitment to professional development, scholarship, and service to the university and community.
Demonstrated self-awareness of one's own cultural beliefs, perspectives, and privileges as a part of one's orientation towards teaching.
Demonstrated decision-making that is informed by research, data, and theory and that leverages students' unique cultures, experiences, and background as strengths.

The pay range for this position is $50,469-$63,086 for the assistant professor level and $58,862-$73,578 for those with experience at the associate professor level. Salary offers will be based on experience and education. For detailed benefits information please visit our Human Resources Benefits Page.
